results.content: This is a horizontal bar chart showing how 1,461 U.S. registered voters described President Trump in a Sept. 11–14, 2026, Economist/YouGov poll. The most commonly selected descriptions were “corrupt” (53%) and “dangerous” (51%), followed by “out-of-touch” (47%), “cruel” (46%), and “bold” and “racist” (45% each). Fewer voters described Trump as “strong” (37%), “intelligent” (35%), “effective” (33%), “honest” (23%), “inspiring” (19%), or “steady” (18%). [...] Methodology: This Economist-sponsored poll was taken September 11-14, 2026. Respondents were selected from YouGov's opt-in panel to be representative of adult U.S. citizens, and screened for voter registration. The margin of error is ± 3.

results.content: Donald Trump's popularity rebounded slightly in this week's Economist / YouGov Poll after his recent slump, but he remains deeply unpopular. This week's poll finds that 36% of Americans strongly or somewhat approve of Trump's job performance, and 57% disapprove — a net job approval of -21. That's an improvement for Trump from the week before, when 35% approved and 61% disapproved for a net approval of -26. Two weeks ago, Trump hit the lowest job approval numbers of either of his terms: 33% [...] A big component of Trump's increase in net job approval over the past week is a rise in support from Independents, who rose from a net approval of -53 last week to -38 this week. results.content: President Donald Trump’s approval rating found a sort of oasis in the desert, rising after weeks of record lows, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll released on Monday, Sept. The poll found that 35% of Americans approved of the president's job performance, up two percentage points from the previous Reuters/Ipsos tracking poll released in early September. Trump’s slight improvement in the newest poll came after three straight weeks of the lowest approval numbers he had seen in Reuters/Ipsos tracking since his return to the White House in 2025.
